Write an essay on the following topic: Speech is Silver but Silence is Golden
answermarkup: Speech is Silver but Silence is Golden Speech is silver but silence is golden is a proverb which guides us to give more importance to silence over speaking. There are times when it is better to maintain dignified silence than speak and add to the confusion. We should be a good judge of the situation and decide whether we should speak or not. Being thoughtful in our communication is extremely important. Our words can have both positive and negative impacts, so it is important to speak only when we have something meaningful to contribute to a conversation. The wisdom of thinking before acting and speaking is captured in the saying: "Think before you act. Think twice before you speak." Always choose silence if speech is not called for. Before we speak, let us ask ourselves the question suggested by Socrates: "Is it true; is it kind, or is it necessary?" If the answer to even one of these questions is 'No, we should remember that speech is silver, but silence is golden.

markup: Write an essay on the following topic: A GIFT FROM NATURE
answermarkup: A GIFT FROM NATURE When I think about a 'beautiful' region the first image that comes to my mind is that of Goa. I love the beauty of Goa. Not the Goa of the tourists, but the southern part of Goa. If you go there during or just after the monsoon, you will come across small hills covered with a thick carpet of greenery. The air smells delicious and fresh. The umpteen rivers and streams are full of sparkling water. The sun's rays shining on the rippling waters makes it seem as if the night stars have been captured here. The tall, swaying lines of coconut trees give the region a romantic look. At night, the sky is surprisingly clear, and if one goes to any of the clean and spacious beaches, one can lie down on the sand and watch the night sky. The umpteen stars twinkling away makes one wonder who or what is up there. The moon beams lovingly on her children on the earth. And finally, the people of the place-content, happy and pleasant. What more can one want?

markup: Write an essay on the following topic: A VISIT TO A HILL STATION
answermarkup: A VISIT TO A HILL STATION I always await the summer vacation anxiously, for this is the time we go on our annual family trip. Last year we had been to Kashmir. This year we decided to travel down south to Udagamandalam (Ootacamund or Ooty for short). After spending a few days in Bengaluru and Mysuru, we proceeded to Ooty. We went there by bus and the journey was pleasant. The weather began changing halfway up the mountains, but we had equipped ourselves with sweaters, scarves and woollen caps. The road upwards was quite steep, and the tall Nilgiri trees were fascinating. It seemed like we were moving through the clouds. Ooty itself is a beautiful place, full of greenery! We put up at a small but pretty cottage on one of the slopes. The climate was very pleasant and we were full of energy. We went for long walks every day, without getting tired even once. We visited the Botanical Gardens and the Boat Club. The boat ride was sheer fun and the water blue and clear. We saw nearly all the famous mountain points and clicked many photographs. We stayed at Ooty for three whole days and then took the bus back to Mysuru. It took us another two days to reach Nagpur. Here the climate was extremely dry and hot, and we couldn't help remembering the cool heights of Udagamandalam.

markup: Write an essay on the following topic: Autobiography of a Tree
answermarkup: Autobiography of a Tree My ancestors lived in the land 4000 years ago and I am well-known in India and some desert regions. I am a descendant of the 'Divine Tree' class also known as the 'Life-giver'. You may have guessed it by now. I am the 'Neem Tree' - 'Nature's Daughter'. I am evergreen and don't require much water to survive, but plenty of sunlight. My kin are a part of every household's garden in the village. But my kin are also seen in small and big cities. I took birth in the garden of a small bungalow close to the roadside. The owners prayed to me every morning and plucked a few leaves to adorn their puja room and also used me in their kitchen. I was happy that I could serve them. Early morning, the grandfather would pluck a thick stem to brush his teeth. Grandmother would extract some juice and made everyone drink in the morning. From puja nan kitchen - to the bedrooms, I proudly flaunted. I was a terror to the termites in the wooden beds or bugs or insects in the wardrobes and other shelves. I was a healer to the children am adults - if they suffered from any ailments or wounds. I was very happy to be a part of sus a family. But one fine day, a man who called himself a Municipal Officer arrived. He brought s news for the family. He wanted a part of the garden to widen the road. I was on the edge of garden and I would have to leave. I heard the grandfather say that it was the plight of all brethren in villages and cities - We, trees, had no value and importance. Next morning, I was heartbroken. The family prayed to me for the last time. They plucked branches but they could not restore me. I knew my fate! But what can a dumb, speechless can do against the power of man? We give them a healthy life to live well, but they thoughtlessly take our lives! If only man understands, 'We are their life and breath!"

markup: Write an essay on the following topic: TELEVISION : ADVANTAGES AND DISADVANTAGES
answermarkup: TELEVISION : ADVANTAGES AND DISADVANTAGES One of the favourite pastimes of children today is watching TV. They prefer to spend their evenings watching cartoons or serials on TV rather than playing outdoors. This is certainly not good. If viewed for long hours every day it affects their health – particularly the eyesight. But does all this mean that one should not watch TV? No, for TV has its good side too. Science and news-based programmes and quizzes give a lot of information and improve one's general knowledge. Cartoons, good serials and children's programmes can provide a lot of healthy entertainment. One can even see exciting matches and international events while sitting right in one's home! TV is useful for farmers too. There are daily weather forecasts to help them. There are also programmes that give them tips about modern methods of farming. Advertisements make people aware of the different products available. Thus, TV has its advantages as well as its disadvantages. It is up to us to make the best use of this invention and see to it that it turns out to be a boon for us, not a curse.

markup: Write an essay on the following topic: The person I like the most
answermarkup: The person I like the most We all love and like our parents, grandparents, friends. But there is always someone special to us, whom we like the most. The person I like the most is my only brother, Ritesh. He is five years older than me but there is a special bonding between us. As a child, I remember crying and throwing tantrums to possess whatever he owned. My parents would scold him for not sharing, and he would lose his mood. But slowly and gradually, we became friends and I changed. I realised that when I was in Class Five and he was in Class Ten. One day, I suddenly became unconscious in class. The teacher helped me to recover. In the meanwhile, my brother arrived. He caught me tight in his arms and comforted me. He carried me upto the autorickshaw, even though my teacher and peon were there to help me. He took me directly to the doctor. At home, he really pampered me and did not leave my bedside till our parents returned from office. I then realised, how selfish and wicked I had been to deprive him of his fun. Soon we became the best of friends. The doctor advised me to take a few days' rest. It was at that time that he sacrificed his playtime and friends and kept me occupied with indoor games. In these few days, our lives changed. He taught me games on mobile and even helped me with some projects on computer. My brother is in college, but we share and talk about our friends, his college experiences, movies etc. We often go to movies together too. He is a gem of a person and I know I cannot stay without him. 'The bond between us is strong and deep, leaving us memories to treasure and keep.

markup: Write an essay on the following topic: A Journey by Bus
answermarkup: A Journey by Bus 'Life is a journey.' It was a long weekend in August. My parents decided to go to Lonavala by bus. Travelling from Mumbai to Lonavala can be very exciting and especially if you have a window seat. We left Mumbai early Friday morning by Shivneri bus. Being a long weekend, many of them had hit the road to this getaway spot. As soon as we crossed Mumbai, we could feel the fresh air, the cool breeze brushing our cheeks. What a pleasant weather! Slowly, the bus started moving up the ghats. There was traffic ahead. This bus was literally crawling, but we could enjoy the scenic beauty. The curves, the bends and the steep climb blocked my ears for a while. For the first time, I enjoyed the greenery, the tall and majestic Sahyadri mountains. The valleys below, the waterfalls, water gushing down the valley and small streams of water. Looking down, I could see the houses and few tribals moving about. Everything looked so tiny. I wondered how all these would appear from an aeroplane. The bus went up and down the ghats. At times we were at such narrow curves, that I nearly held my father's arms tightly the first time. My sister sitting ahead of me was busy clicking away snaps on her mobile. It had started drizzling. Suddenly we saw a rainbow between the two valleys - Oh what a sight to behold! As we moved a little further, we were enveloped by the clouds which were so low. It looked like white fluffy cotton. The driver slowed down. He had to be cautious and careful. I could feel my heartbeats racing faster than during sports. After a three hours' journey, we finally reached Lonavala 'The Jewel of the Sahyadri'. My heart leaped with joy! The journey was exciting. I was totally mesmerised by the beauty of the landscapes. It did not matter to me who else was on the bus I said to myself, 'If there is Paradise on earth, it is this, it is this!'

markup: Write a dialogue between a child and mother on why self-help is the best help.
answermarkup:
Mom: Ankit, I refuse to help you with the science project. You should do this project yourself. Remember, self-help is the best help.
Ankit: Mom, could you explain the meaning of this proverb?
Mom: 'Self-help is the best help' means that we should do things without depending on others.
Ankit: Why is this important? What is wrong with taking help?
Mom: Self-help is important because when we do things on our own, we understand them better.
Ankit: I remember, Mom, when I completed the earlier project myself, I realised what my strengths and weaknesses are.
Mom: Could you elaborate, Ankit?
Ankit: The last project was on 'Protection of Animals.' I realised that I was good at presenting the information. At the same time, I could improve in the artwork.
Mom: When you do things on your own, you realise the importance of your own efforts. You become more confident. You learn from your mistakes too.
Ankit: Thank you, Mom, for your advice. I will try to be independent at all times.

markup: Imagine you are Sayali. Write your diary for every day of your trip to the moon. and for the day you gave the earrings to your mother.
answermarkup:
Day 1: Arrived at 7.30 a.m. Flight was simply amazing! Out of this world! Already worth every rupee that Mom has spent. Settled down, unpacked. Am in a dormitory with three other girls. Were given instructions and precautions. Next programme: Skywatch. FANTASTIC! SUPERB! Am wonderstruck at the brilliance of the stars and the earth. Mom just has to make this trip.
Afternoon, saw the settlements inside. Much like earth settlements, though people are fewer. Then 2 hours of self-study and writing - can't escape that even here! Bed. Tired but thrilled.
Day 2: First explored area near camp. Interesting people and shops. Shops are costly. Then the CIRCUS! Oh my! The way those gymnasts jumped and swung! Of course, it was easier than on earth, as the moon's gravitational force is 1/6 that of earth. Still, my heart was in my mouth in fear. After that, once again went to another set of settlements. Far from the main center. People here more like the tribals on earth. Then homework again and bed.
Day 3: Spent morning visiting the place where Neil Armstrong landed so many many years ago. Oldest place in the history of man on the moon. Wonder how people did it in those days with their limited technology. Saw statue of Armstrong and his famous words, 'One small step......'. Later visited the research lab. Bit boring and technical Then finally, FINALLY went outside the artificially maintained environment into the atmosphere of the moon. Wore space suits which felt heavy first and then as light as air. Wonderful, wonderful experience. Saw many roadside shops, just like on earth. Saw some beautiful earrings and remembered Mom. Love her. Want to take something for her. Will buy the earrings.
Day 4: Oh no, oh no, oh no! Showed the earrings to Mom. She picked them up. She exclaimed that they were terribly heavy. Remembered that I had bought them from that cheating shopkeeper in the field of the moon's gravity. Foolish me! Oh, never mind, says Mum, she will keep them in the cupboard and look at them every day. Thanks Mom.

markup: You are appointed as a class monitor for the first time. Write your feelings of your new role on the first day.

markup: Write a dialogue between your teacher and you about the true meaning of happiness.
answermarkup:
Teacher: Yogen, can you explain to me what true happiness means to you?
Yogen: Yes, teacher. In my opinion happiness lies in those moments when we experience joy.
Teacher: You are partially right. But remember, true happiness lies in living a life committed to doing good.
Yogen: What are the ways in which we can be happy, teacher?
Teacher: Doing things which you like and being with people who bring out the best in you are ways to remain happy.
Yogen : Yes. I am the happiest when I am with my friends and my family. I also experience happiness when I am on the field playing cricket.
Teacher: What are the situations wherein you experience happiness?
Yogen: I experience happiness when I help others. I remember the happiest day of my life was when I rescued an injured animal and took it to the veterinary hospital. 
Teacher: So happy to hear this. Yes, happiness lies in service, too. We should find joy in service.
Yogen: Thank you for your words of wisdom, teacher. Your words never fail to inspire me. Have a nice day!

Romel: Discipline is indeed an . important quality that each one of us should develop in order to succeed.

markup: Prepare a diary entry of a boy who gets a surprise birthday gift from her parents.
answermarkup:
15 September, 2023
Dear Diary,
It was that day of the year again, 15 September, my birthday. I got up in the morning and realised that there was absolutely no excitement in the air. It appeared to be just like any other ordinary day. I feared my parents had forgotten my birthday.
Heartbroken, I went to school. Rohan, my best friend, wished me. He, too, did not discuss my birthday any further. After a long day at school, I went back home dejected and depressed. I rang the bell and my mother opened the door.
As I entered the drawing room, there was a moment of silence. Suddenly, the room filled with the cheerful chorus of "Happy Birthday" from Rohan and my other friends. My mom told me to change into party clothes and what followed was great fun, frolic and excitement. After cake cutting, everyone enjoyed the good food my mom had prepared for the party.
What a memorable evening it was! As the last of my friends left, my parents gave me a gift box. With great excitement, I opened it. And what did I find in it? A beautiful telescope. For a sky watcher like me, this was just what I wanted. My parents knew that observing moons and stars is my hobby and they made my day all the more special with this thoughtful gift.
With a heart full of happiness, I end my diary entry for today.
Aman

markup: One Saturday, your class teacher and all of you planned a programme called 'Seeing Eyes, Helping Hands' to get involved in social service projects. One of your friends was absent that day. markup: Write a dialogue between two friends who have a Geography test in the class that day.
answermarkup:
Navin: Hello, Govind! How have you prepared for today's Geography test?
Govind: Not very well. I've yet to go through paragraph answers.
Navin: Why, what happened? Didn't you find time yesterday to study?
Govind: No, we had guests at home. My mummy sent me to the shop to buy snacks for them. Also a small boy of about 3 years had come along. He didn't allow me to study.
Navin: You could have told your mother that you wanted to study.
Govind: I could have, but then she would have scolded me saying as to what I had been doing all these days without doing my daily lessons.
Navin: That's quite right! Why don't you do your daily lessons regularly? I do my studies regularly. I revise all the lessons done during the working days on Sundays. So, I get enough revisions done before the tests begin. At least, from now onwards do your daily lessons regularly. Then you won't have to worry about any unexpected occupation at the 11th hour.
Govind: Very true! What you're saying is correct. I'll also follow your method of studying. Will you help me, Navin, with the map work for the test?
Navin: Definitely. Bring the outline map of India. I'll teach you the easiest way to locate the places to be marked.
Govind: Thank you, Navin. You're very relaxed. Next time onwards, you'll find me relaxed before the tests. Come on, take this map. Tell me, what do I do? (Both the boys sit with the map, and Navin begins to teach him.)

markup: Imagine you are the Students' Representative. Prepare a notice to be put up on the school notice-board, encouraging the students to take active participation in the Canteen Day celebrations to be held in the school campus.
answermarkup: COME, ENJOY! MOTHER'S RECIPES! Canteen Day will be held in the school premises for standard V to X. Date: 6th December, 2017 Time: 9.30 a.m. to 11.30 a.m. Students interested to open stalls should enrol their names with their class teachers. Only home-made food items are allowed for sale. Cost should not exceed Rs. 10/- per item. Sd/- Students' Representative 20th November, 2017
